post.description:
Create new user with PKI certificate authentication

The certificate file will be parsed to extract:
- Common Name (CN)
- Serial Number
- SHA256 Fingerprint

These fields are hashed before storage for security.

Parameters:
- certificate: PKI certificate file (PEM or DER format)
- username: Unique username (3-50 characters)
- username_alias: Display name (1-255 characters)
- role_ids: JSON array string of role IDs, e.g. "[1, 2, 3]"
- post_id: Optional post/position ID

get.description: Available filter params and sortable fields for tags.

List observations with attached media IDs and comprehensive filtering.
Regular users can only see observations from their assigned post.
Admins can see all observations or filter by specific post.

Filters (all optional):
- Basic: post_id, status
- Absolute dates: observed_at_from, observed_at_to
- Relative dates: last_n_days (e.g., 3 = last 3 days including today)
                  day_offset (e.g., 0=today, 1=yesterday, 2=day before)
- skip_empty_days: Skip days with no observations (for relative date queries)
- Pagination: skip, limit (if not provided, returns all matching records)

Examples:
- Get all observations: /observations
- Get last 7 days: /observations?last_n_days=7
- Get yesterday's data: /observations?day_offset=1
- Get specific date range: /observations?observed_at_from=2025-01-01&observed_at_to=2025-01-31
- Paginated: /observations?skip=0&limit=100

DB Load: Uses eager loading (selectinload) to fetch media_files in a single additional query,
preventing N+1 query problem. For N observations, this executes 2 queries instead of N+1.

get.description: Get storage statistics and health information

post.description:
Upload a complete file with comprehensive validation and security checks.
Users can only upload files for observations from their assigned post.

Upload a file via Nginx offloading (client_body_in_file_only).

Nginx receives the raw file body, writes it to a temp file on disk, and
forwards the temp file path to FastAPI via the X-File-Name header.
FastAPI validates the file, moves it to storage, and cleans up the temp file.
The file is never loaded entirely into memory.

Client sends raw binary body (not multipart form) with metadata in query params
and the original filename in the X-Original-Filename header.
